summary: Investigation confirmed global PostgreSQL database connection pool saturation. Diagnostic procedures query pg_stat_activity for client connections and idle in transaction sessions, and mandate configuring PgBouncer in transaction pooling mode to allocate server connections only during active transaction execution, preventing microservices from holding persistent idle connections.

findings.finding: Global PostgreSQL database connection pool reached saturation with remaining connection slots reserved for superuser connections. Query pg_stat_activity to inspect client connections and idle in transaction sessions.

Operational guide [KB-1] instructs querying pg_stat_activity to inspect client connections and idle in transaction sessions, and configuring PgBouncer in transaction pooling mode to allocate server connections only during active transaction execution, preventing microservices from holding persistent idle connections.

probable_root_cause: Persistent idle client connections from unpooled microservices saturating server max_connections.
recommendations: Query pg_stat_activity to inspect client connection states and counts.
Terminate idle in transaction sessions exceeding 60 seconds.
Configure PgBouncer in transaction pooling mode to prevent microservices from holding persistent idle connections.
